findings.failure_path: The gate scans JSON from the current specs working tree and passes each matching ledger to the validator without checking that the ledger or its referenced receipts are tracked and byte-identical to HEAD. An earlier CI command can therefore generate or modify candidate-bound evidence after checkout; the gate accepts it even though the evidence was never committed or reviewable in the landing diff.
findings.smallest_fix: Before scanning, fail if the evidence root has tracked modifications or untracked files, and consider only regular files tracked by HEAD; equivalently, validate the ledger and every referenced evidence blob from a temporary HEAD tree rather than the mutable worktree. Add tests for both untracked and modified candidate-bound evidence.

findings.failure_path: The enforcement step runs only when github.event_name is pull_request. A direct/admin push or merge_group execution skips it, so the enclosing CI job can pass without producing the script's required unevaluated failure. The diff supplies no branch-protection configuration proving that such landing paths are impossible.
findings.smallest_fix: Run the gate for every landing-capable event with an event-appropriate, fetched base (for example pull_request.base.sha, merge-group base, or push before SHA) and let missing/unresolvable bases fail unevaluated; otherwise include and verify external required-check/branch-protection evidence that makes non-PR landings impossible.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Succession and ledger phase-binding implement the intended three-round/two-chain shape, but the merge gate can accept runtime-generated evidence and is skipped entirely outside pull_request events.
Evidence is read from the mutable working tree without proving it is committed, allowing untracked or modified ledger artifacts to satisfy a merge-control boundary.
The script fails closed when invoked without a base, but the workflow bypasses that behavior by not invoking it on non-pull-request landings.
The tests cover candidate mismatch, invalid ledgers, option-shaped bases, and tree perturbation, but never test untracked/modified evidence or workflow event bypasses.
Historical per-chain budget-one receipts remain structurally compatible; however, restricting enforcement to pull_request leaves push and merge-group workflows behaviorally unprotected.
No migration is required, but the packet contains no branch-protection or required-check evidence supporting the assumption that every landing must pass a pull-request execution of this step.
Invoked failures identify the required candidate and rejected ledgers, while skipped workflow events produce no unevaluated diagnostic and can leave the enclosing job green.
The autonomous succession is bounded and one-shot, but merge enforcement remains bypassable through mutable, uncommitted evidence and through landing paths where the conditional step is skipped.
